response.title: which robot mowers are safest around kids and dogs
response.answer:
When choosing a robot lawn mower for a yard shared with kids and dogs, I'd prioritize safety over cutting performance, navigation accuracy, or price.

The most important distinction is between mowers that merely stop when they hit something and mowers that detect people and animals before making contact.

Even the best robot mower is not safe enough to operate unattended while children or pets are playing on the lawn.

What makes a robot mower safer?

I'd look for these features, in this order:

Camera-based obstacle detection: Recognizes people, pets, and objects before contact.

Reliable automatic blade stopping: Stops cutting when lifted, tilted, or triggered by a safety sensor.

Protected cutting blades: Recessed blades and a guarded cutting deck reduce accidental contact.

Small-object detection: Important for dog paws, tails, toys, and objects lying in the grass.

Scheduling and remote controls: Lets you mow only when kids and dogs are indoors, with an easy way to pause operation.

A critical detail: a mower advertised as having AI obstacle avoidance isn't necessarily proven to detect a child's hand or a small dog lying in the grass.

My top robot mower choices for families in 2026

These are my strongest candidates based on obstacle-avoidance technology and available hands-on testing, not a certified ranking of injury risk.

Shop
Best for small family yards

Mammotion YUKA mini 2 LiDAR

Combines LiDAR and AI vision. Independent testing found it avoided small balls, gloves, and other low-profile objects particularly well.

Why I'd consider it: Strong evidence of detecting the sorts of toys children leave outside. 
The Hook Up
+1

Shop

Mammotion LUBA 3 AWD

Best for large or sloped yards

Uses 360° LiDAR and dual-camera AI vision. Hands-on reviewers reported successful avoidance of dog toys, balls, branches, and other obstacles.

Why I'd consider it: A sophisticated sensing system with encouraging real-world testing. 
The Hook Up
+1

Shop

Segway Navimow H2

Promising for dog owners

Combines LiDAR, vision, and positioning technology. A hands-on review of the H206E reported that it reliably avoided a dog, toys, and garden obstacles.

Why I'd consider it: Actual dog-avoidance observations, although not a controlled safety certification. 
Robovations

NAVIMOW i215 8.6 in. Robot Lawn Mower (3/8 Acre) LiDAR + Vis…

Alternative for medium yards

$1,399.00 at The Home Depot

Uses LiDAR and vision for obstacle avoidance. However, one two-month review reported it ran over a small ball, so I would rank it below the strongest small-object performers for a toy-filled lawn. 
Tom's Guide

What I would actually buy

For a small suburban yard, I'd start with the Mammotion YUKA mini 2. For a large, uneven yard, I'd investigate the LUBA 3 AWD. If your main concern is a dog that sometimes wanders into the mowing area, the Navimow H2 is also worth serious consideration.

Consumer Reports' 2026 testing explicitly evaluates obstacle detection, pets, foot-contact scenarios, and automatic blade stopping. It recommends keeping children off the lawn during operation regardless of the mower's safety rating. 
Consumer Reports
+1

Are you primarily concerned about:

Young children accidentally approaching or touching the mower
Dogs walking, running, or lying in the grass
Both children and dogs

Under ¼ acre
¼–½ acre
Over ½ acre
Narrow down the safest models
